cards.name: Noise
cards.summary: Adds random per-pixel noise to the clip, either coloured or monochrome. The noise re-randomises every frame on its own, so it moves without keyframes.
use_for: Light mono grain (3-6) on an adjustment layer to glue AI or stock shots into one documentary look
Match clean graphics or screen recordings to noisy archival footage in an explainer
Short noise burst on a cut as a cheap glitch / signal-loss transition in a news reel
CCTV / surveillance-style texture on a clearly labelled reconstruction or dramatisation (never to pass staged footage off as real CCTV in news)
Light grain to blend AI-generated or clean stock shots with archive footage
Gritty texture on documentary reenactments
Heavy static for glitch/TV-off hits in reels and trailers
Break up banding in gradients and dark title backgrounds
avoid: Colour noise above ~15 on faces: looks like a broken sensor, not film grain
Heavy noise before export to social: platform compression smears it into blocky mush and wastes bitrate
Turning off Clip Result Values with high amounts: values wrap and produce harsh coloured specks
Above ~10% on full-frame shots it reads as bad video, and grain balloons file size and compresses poorly on Instagram
Colour noise looks digital, not filmic; switch Use Color Noise off for film grain

params.name: Amount of Noise
params.does: Strength of the noise in percent
params.typical: 3-6 subtle grain; 20-40 obvious texture; 60+ glitch burst

params.name: Use Color Noise
params.does: On = independent RGB noise (coloured specks); off = luminance-only mono noise

params.name: Clip Result Values
params.does: Clamps noisy pixels to legal values instead of letting them wrap around

cards.scripting: Use Color Noise and Clip Result Values are real booleans in the Premiere harvest (AE exposes them as 0/1). Amount of Noise is 0-100. Put it on an adjustment layer above a section so all clips share one grain. GPU: the install ships an AEFX_Noise GPU kernel, so treat it as accelerated.

verified.note: Coloured speckle grain now covers the whole frame (mean diff 8.2/255 vs 4.4 at Amount 40): a gritty low-light texture at gallery size and clearly RGB noise when zoomed.

cards.merged: 2026-10-13: the duplicate card in pr_effect_05.json was merged here; use_for / avoid (and look, pairs_with, sources) are the union, and that card is kept whole in merged_from

merged_from.name: Noise
merged_from.summary: Adds random pixel noise (colour or monochrome) to the clip, from subtle film-like grain to heavy TV static.
use_for: Light grain to blend AI-generated or clean stock shots with archive footage
Gritty texture on documentary reenactments
Heavy static for glitch/TV-off hits in reels and trailers
Break up banding in gradients and dark title backgrounds
avoid: Above ~10% on full-frame shots it reads as bad video, and grain balloons file size and compresses poorly on Instagram
Colour noise looks digital, not filmic; switch Use Color Noise off for film grain

params.name: Amount of Noise
params.does: Percent of noise added

params.name: Use Color Noise
params.does: Coloured noise per channel (true) or monochrome (false)

params.name: Clip Result Values
params.does: Clips values so noise cannot wrap around to odd colours

merged_from.scripting: Amount of Noise is a percent (0-100). For grain on a whole sequence put it on an adjustment layer. The noise pattern is regenerated every frame automatically; no keyframes are needed for moving grain.

verified.note: At Amount 60 a visible colour grain covers the whole frame (walls, faces, stripes), clearly gritty against the clean reference.

cards.name: Offset
cards.summary: Slides the image inside its frame and wraps whatever leaves one edge back in from the opposite edge, like a tiled texture. Blend With Original mixes the shifted copy over the untouched image.
use_for: Fast keyframed Offset plus Directional Blur as a whip/slide transition between two shots in a reel
Endless horizontal scroll of a map, ticker strip or texture background in an explainer
Seamless looping background plate for titles
Quick glitch-style frame shift on a beat in a news promo
avoid: Slow offsets on live-action: the visible wrap seam looks like a mistake
Using it as a transition without motion blur: the shift reads as a jump, not a whip

params.name: Shift Center To
params.does: Where the image centre is moved to; the image wraps around the frame edges
params.typical: [0.5, 0.5] = no shift; [1.5, 0.5] = one full width, looks identical (loop point)

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix of the original image back over the shifted one (harvested as a 0-1 fraction)
params.typical: 0 for a clean wrap; 0.5 for a double-exposure ghost

cards.scripting: Effects-panel bin is Transform in the installed v26 plugin (older Premiere versions listed Offset under Distort). Points are frame fractions; values beyond 0..1 should be accepted (the image just wraps more times) but the harvest gave no point range, so verify a value like 2.5 reads back before building a whip on it. A shift of exactly one frame width/height lands on an identical frame, which is the trick for a seamless whip: shift by whole widths so start and end match. Blend With Original is 0-1 (UI shows %). GPU kernel 'Offset' ships with the install.

verified.note: Image slid right by 30% with the right-hand side (a figure and the plant) wrapped back in on the left, leaving a hard vertical seam at about x=30%.

cards.name: Posterize
cards.summary: Reduces the number of tonal levels per colour channel, turning smooth gradients into flat bands of colour like a screen print or poster.
use_for: Stylised pop-art look on a politician's portrait for a satire or explainer title card
Graphic, comic-style treatment of a stock clip behind bold text
Retro low-bit look for a meme or gaming segment in a reel
avoid: Low levels on noisy or compressed footage: bands crawl and flicker frame to frame
Skin at low levels looks blotchy unless that is the intent

params.name: Level
params.does: Number of tonal levels per channel

cards.scripting: Single property Level, 2-255 (default 7). A light blur or Median before it gives cleaner, less noisy bands. Keyframing Level from 255 down reads as a stepped reveal, not a smooth fade.

verified.note: Smooth tones collapsed into flat green, orange, maroon and pink bands; it reads as a screen print, as described.

cards.name: Posterize Time
cards.summary: Locks the clip to a lower frame rate so motion becomes choppy and stepped, like stop-motion or a dropped-frame feed.
use_for: Stop-motion / cut-out feel on animated graphics or maps in an explainer (6-12 fps)
Stutter on a beat drop or a dramatic reveal in a trailer
Fake glitchy live-feed or CCTV look in a news reel
avoid: On talking heads for more than a beat: lip-sync looks broken
Expecting it to show on a still image or a static shot: there is nothing to step

params.name: Frame Rate
params.does: Frame rate the clip is held to

cards.scripting: Only visible on moving footage or animated layers; the demo frame of a still photo will look unchanged, which is expected. Premiere applies the clip's intrinsic Motion/Opacity after its effects, so Motion keyframes on the same clip still animate smoothly: to step an animated graphic, nest it and apply Posterize Time to the nest. Time effects on an adjustment layer are unreliable in Premiere (it may not step the layers below), so prefer nesting and render-test. Frame Rate harvested range is ~0.01-99; values at or above the sequence rate change nothing.

verified.note: Still matches the reference as expected (1.0 s lands on a held frame); in builds/pve_pr_gallery_045_pr.mp4 at 24-26 s each image is held for 4 frames with zero change between, i.e. stepped ~6 fps motion.

cards.name: ProcAmp
cards.summary: Broadcast-style processing amplifier: one-stop brightness, contrast, hue rotation and saturation, with an optional split-screen before/after.
use_for: Fast saturation drop to near-zero for a flashback or archival-style segment in a documentary
Quick contrast/saturation punch on dull stock clips in a reel
Animated drain-to-black-and-white on a freeze-frame before a reveal or 'fact check' card
Split Screen on to show before/after of a grade
avoid: Brightness lifts blacks to grey (it is an offset, not a gamma); use Lumetri for real grading
Large Hue rotations on people: skin turns green or blue

params.name: Brightness
params.does: Adds or subtracts a constant to all pixels

params.name: Contrast
params.does: Contrast in percent, 100 = unchanged

params.name: Hue
params.does: Rotates all hues, in degrees
params.typical: 0; +-10 to nudge; 180 for an inverted-colour stylisation

params.name: Saturation
params.does: Saturation in percent, 100 = unchanged, 0 = black and white

params.name: Split Screen
params.does: Shows the effect on only part of the frame for before/after

params.name: Split Percent
params.does: Where the split line sits, percent of width

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color (modern Premiere route); AE: Hue/Saturation + Brightness & Contrast
cards.scripting: Contrast and Saturation are percents where 100 = neutral (range 0-200); Brightness -100..100; Hue is degrees (harvested range is the raw -32768..32767, keep within -180..180). Remember to leave Split Screen false on final renders.

verified.note: Hue +45 turns the cream walls and skin green and the red stripes orange, with visibly higher saturation and contrast: the hue-shift / boosted-colour look the card describes.

cards.name: RGB Difference Key
cards.summary: Old simple colour keyer (lives in Premiere's Obsolete bin): makes pixels close to a chosen colour transparent, with a basic similarity threshold and None/Low/High edge smoothing. Ultra Key does the same job far better.
use_for: Quick-and-dirty removal of a flat, evenly lit coloured background from a graphic or logo
Legacy projects that already use it
avoid: Any green-screen talking head or presenter: no spill suppression, hard aliased edges; use Ultra Key
Unevenly lit or compressed backgrounds: holes and fringes appear

params.name: Color
params.does: Background colour to key out
params.typical: #00B140 for a green screen, sampled from the plate

params.name: Similarity
params.does: How far from the key colour pixels can be and still drop out

params.name: Smoothing
params.does: Edge anti-aliasing amount (dropdown)

cards.scripting: Verified from the installed plugin: category Obsolete; Smoothing menu is None|Low|High (0-2). The two unnamed boolean rows are Mask Only and Drop Shadow, in that order; they cannot be addressed by name. Demo keys out near-white areas (they turn transparent/black), which only proves the effect runs; for real work use Ultra Key.

verified.note: At Similarity 60 the near-white areas (white stripes, lamps, wall highlights, a small round motif) drop out as jagged black holes, a hard colour key with aliased edges as described.

cards.name: Ramp
cards.summary: Generates a linear or radial colour gradient between two points and colours, replacing the clip's image unless blended back with the original.
use_for: Gradient background plate for title cards, quote cards and lower thirds in explainers
Bottom-darkening scrim behind captions in a reel: white-to-black Ramp on a Color Matte above the footage, blend mode Multiply
Saffron-to-green or brand-colour wash over a stock shot for a political promo
Radial ramp as a cheap spotlight / vignette layer
avoid: Applying it straight to footage with Blend With Original 0: the shot is completely replaced
Wide, subtle gradients on 8-bit export without Ramp Scatter: visible banding after compression

params.name: Start of Ramp
params.does: Where the start colour sits

params.name: Start Color
params.does: Colour at the start point

params.name: End of Ramp
params.does: Where the end colour sits

params.name: End Color
params.does: Colour at the end point

params.name: Ramp Shape
params.does: Linear or radial gradient (dropdown)
params.typical: 0 linear; 1 radial from the start point

params.name: Ramp Scatter
params.does: Dithers the gradient to hide banding

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mixes the original image back in (0-1 fraction)
params.typical: 0 on a colour matte; 0.5-0.7 as a wash over footage

cards.scripting: Points are frame fractions; Blend With Original is a 0-1 fraction (UI shows %), so 0 = pure gradient. Ramp Shape menu verified as Linear Ramp|Radial Ramp. Ramp makes no transparency: for a caption scrim put it on a Color Matte with Start Color #FFFFFF at [0.5, 0.55], End Color #000000 at [0.5, 1], blend mode Multiply, opacity 60-80. Start/End Color defaults are black/white. GPU kernel 'Ramp' ships with the install.

verified.note: Orange-to-deep-purple linear gradient runs top to bottom over the shot, blended at 40% so the people stay readable.

cards.name: Replicate
cards.summary: Tiles the whole clip into a grid of identical copies (Count x Count) inside the frame.
use_for: Video-wall / wall-of-TVs look for a news montage or media-coverage segment
Grid transition on a beat: snap from one image to a 3x3 wall of it in a reel
Repeating a logo or face for a 'everyone is saying this' satire beat
avoid: Small tiles of busy footage on a phone screen: nothing is readable
Expecting different clips per tile: every tile is the same clip

params.name: Count
params.does: Number of tiles per row and column (2 = 2x2 = 4 copies)

cards.scripting: Count is an integer 2-16 per side; there is no 1 (remove the effect to get a single image). Count steps are hard cuts when keyframed, so animate a grid reveal by keyframing Scale on a nest instead.

verified.note: Frame tiled into a 3x3 grid of identical copies (video-wall look).

cards.name: Pixel Motion Blur
cards.summary: Adds realistic motion blur to footage by tracking pixel movement between frames (optical flow) and smearing along it, for shots that were shot or rendered with too little blur.
use_for: Make sped-up timelapse or fast-forward crowd footage look natural instead of strobing
Add blur to AI-generated or CGI shots that came out crisp and jittery
Smooth a speed-ramped action beat in a trailer
Soften strobing on fast pans shot with a high shutter speed
avoid: Shots with overlapping motion (crossing people, waving flags in front of faces): optical flow tears and warps edges
Static shots: nothing happens, but it still costs render time

Unattended scripted exports: in PVE's Premiere 2026 H.264 renders this effect failed in all eight attempts, three at Shutter Angle 720 / 16 samples and five more at 360 / 8 (software 'Software effect returned error', GPU 'Unable to process frame'), while Timewarp's Pixel Motion from the same plugin rendered fine; keep it out of automated builds until a manual render of it succeeds

params.name: Shutter Control
params.does: Manual (use Shutter Angle) or Automatic (follows host motion-blur settings, which Premiere does not have) (dropdown)

params.name: Shutter Angle
params.does: Amount of blur; 180 = natural film shutter, higher = longer smear

params.name: Shutter Samples
params.does: Quality of the blur (more samples = smoother, slower)

params.name: Vector Detail
params.does: Density of motion vectors analysed

cards.scripting: Only visible on footage with motion; a still shot shows no change (expected). Shutter Control order verified from the installed plugin strings (Manual|Automatic): 0 = Manual, the default, so Shutter Angle applies. Ships inside Premiere's AEFilterRollingShutter plugin with category Time and is applied fine by script, but it may not be listed in the Effects panel (not verified). CPU optical-flow effect: slow, render-test a short range first.

verified.note: No frame exists: Premiere refused to export it every time (pr_v1 builds 063, 063_v2, 063_v3 at 720 / 16; builds 060, 060_v2, 060_v3, 061, 061_v2 at 360 / 8: Software effect returned error, then GPU Unable to process frame) and it is in gallery/pr/failed.json, so the shutter values are not the cause.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: verdict not_rendered -> broken (a refused render, same convention as AE failed.json); status current -> unusable, since 8/8 scripted exports failed and 'current' keeps it in gallery reruns and boosts it in pve find; attempt count fixed (3 at 720/16 + 5 at 360/8, not five in all)

cards.name: Rolling Shutter Repair
cards.summary: Corrects the jello / skew distortion that CMOS cameras and phones produce during fast pans or vibration, by analysing motion and un-warping each scanline.
use_for: Fix wobbly phone footage of rallies, protests or crowds shot on the move
Straighten leaning buildings and poles in fast handheld or drone pans for a documentary
Clean up vibration jello in car-mounted or helicopter footage before stabilising
avoid: Footage without rolling-shutter artefacts: it can introduce subtle warping
Applying after scaling, speed changes or stabilisation: apply it first on the source clip

params.name: Rolling Shutter Rate
params.does: Fraction of the frame time spent scanning; matches the camera's readout
params.typical: 50-70 for most DSLR/mirrorless cameras; close to 100 for phones; tweak until verticals go straight

params.name: Scan Direction
params.does: Direction the sensor reads out (dropdown)

params.name: Method
params.does: Warp (faster) or Pixel Motion (more accurate, slower) (dropdown)

params.name: Pixel Motion Detail
params.does: Vector density used by the Pixel Motion method

cards.scripting: Only does anything on footage with rolling-shutter skew from motion; the demo on a still shot will look unchanged (expected). It analyses the clip after being applied; render only after analysis finishes. Pixel Motion Detail matters only when Method = 1. 'Advanced' and 'Advanced#2' are group markers; the unnamed boolean between Method and Pixel Motion Detail is the Detailed Analysis checkbox (Warp method), not addressable by name. Warp Stabilizer also has its own rolling-shutter option, so do not stack both corrections blindly. Scan Direction and Method labels verified from the installed plugin strings. Measured on a 300 px/s pan with a synthetic 48 px skew (live wave 3): the correction is about Rolling Shutter Rate % of one frame of pan motion (Rate 80: 9.5 px of 1920, Rate 100: 10-12 px), which is all a real sensor can skew (readout time <= one frame); the test plate's extra skew stayed, as it should.

verified.note: On the skewed pan the bars stand straighter than in the control slot (skew down from 39 to 29 px of 1920 on average, Rate 100): it removes rolling-shutter skew, up to one frame of pan motion.

previous.why: the test footage has nothing for it to act on (see note), so the render could not show it doing its job
judged on the live wave 3 re-render on the second (synthetic) footage set, which has what the card acts on
previous.note: Frame (and every frame of builds/pve_pr_gallery_062_pr.mp4) matches the untouched clip within encode noise (mean diff 1-3.8/255) because the test clip has no rolling-shutter skew; Rate is already at its 100 maximum, so no demo value can fix it and status is now needs_input (needs skewed phone/handheld footage).

cards.name: Timewarp
cards.summary: Retimes the clip from inside an effect, with keyframable speed (or a direct source-frame map) and optical-flow frame interpolation plus optional synthetic motion blur, for smooth slow motion and speed ramps.
use_for: Smooth slow-motion on a key moment (handshake, crowd wave, slogan) in a documentary or trailer
Keyframed speed ramp (fast-slow-fast) on an action beat in a reel
Freeze-style hold by mapping Source Frame to a constant in Source Frame mode
Interpolated slow-mo for footage shot at only 25/30 fps
avoid: Pixel Motion on shots with crossing objects, waving flags or hair: rubbery warping artefacts
Speeds above 100 on a clip with no extra media after it: frames run out and hold
Expecting the timeline clip to change length: Timewarp retimes inside the clip, the clip duration stays the same

params.name: Method
params.does: How in-between frames are made (dropdown)
params.typical: 2 Pixel Motion for smooth slow-mo; 1 Frame Mix if Pixel Motion warps

params.name: Adjust Time By
params.does: Drive timing by Speed or by direct Source Frame mapping (dropdown)

params.name: Speed
params.does: Playback speed in percent of the source

params.name: Source Frame
params.does: Which source frame to show when Adjust Time By = Source Frame

params.name: Vector Detail
params.does: Motion-vector density for Pixel Motion

params.name: Filtering
params.does: Normal or Extreme quality interpolation (dropdown)

params.name: Shutter Angle
params.does: Synthetic motion-blur amount when motion blur is enabled

params.name: Shutter Samples
params.does: Motion-blur quality

params.name: Shutter Control
params.does: Manual (Shutter Angle) or Automatic motion-blur shutter (dropdown)

cards.scripting: Only visible on moving footage; the still-shot demo looks unchanged (expected). Many rows are group markers that repeat their name (Tuning, Smoothing, Weighting, Motion Blur, Source Crops each appear twice as booleans): ignore them. The unnamed booleans are, in order, Build From One Image, Correct Luminance Changes and Enable Motion Blur: none is addressable by name, so Shutter Angle/Samples do nothing until motion blur is switched on by hand. All menu labels verified from the installed plugin strings. Matte Layer and Warp Layer are layer references with a nonsense harvested range: not settable from a spec. Ships inside Premiere's AEFilterRollingShutter plugin with category Time and applies fine by script, but it may not be listed in the Effects panel (not verified). Prefer Premiere's own Speed/Duration with Optical Flow or Time Remapping for simple constant slow-mo; use Timewarp when a keyframed Speed curve or Source Frame map is needed. CPU-only, slow.

verified.note: Frame at clip time 1.0 s matches source time ~1.2 s (diff 4.5 vs 32 against the 2.0 s reference), i.e. 25% speed, and the render shows smooth interpolated in-betweens.

cards.name: Roughen Edges
cards.summary: Eats into the clip's alpha edges with fractal noise to make torn, eroded, rusty or photocopied borders; on a full-frame opaque clip it roughens the frame border.
use_for: Torn-paper cutout look for photos and newspaper clippings in a documentary or explainer collage
Distressed, grungy edges on title text or logos (apply to the graphic layer)
Ragged border on a scaled-down picture-in-picture for a scrapbook / evidence-board style
Animated boiling edges with keyframed Evolution for a hand-made stop-motion feel
avoid: Huge Border values on small text: letters dissolve and become unreadable
Expecting it to change the interior of a full-frame shot: it works only on alpha edges

params.name: Edge Type
params.does: Style of edge erosion (dropdown)
params.typical: 0 Roughen; 1 Roughen Color for a coloured torn rim; 6 Photocopy

params.name: Edge Color
params.does: Colour of the edge band for the 'Color' edge types

params.name: Border
params.does: How far into the layer the roughness reaches, in pixels

params.name: Edge Sharpness
params.does: Soft vs crisp eroded edge

params.name: Scale
params.does: Size of the fractal detail

params.name: Complexity
params.does: Fractal detail layers

params.name: Evolution
params.does: Animates the fractal pattern (degrees)

params.name: Random Seed
params.does: Picks a different random pattern
params.typical: any integer to vary duplicate layers

cards.scripting: Works on alpha: for a photo cutout, scale the clip down (Motion) or crop it first so it has edges inside the frame; on the full-frame demo only a thick ragged border appears. Edge Type menu verified from the installed plugin strings (8 items, 0-based here). 'Random Seed' is the number; 'Random Seed#2' and 'Evolution Options' are group-marker booleans, ignore them. Offset (Turbulence) is a frame-fraction point. Edge Color only shows with the Color edge types (1, 5, 7). GPU kernels for RoughenEdges ship with the install.

verified.note: Frame border eaten into a ragged, torn black edge all round while the interior stays untouched, as the summary says for a full-frame clip.
